Verify live on 25599: RCON-set night (RCON 25598, password in ~/minecraft/localserver/setup.sh), sealed dig-in, a batch runs and banks stone, a summoned threat interrupts within ~1 s, seal never opens upward. Commit `-- survival.js FEEDBACK.md ...`.
- Then **5q (#125)** EAT/REFLEX ownership thrash (hysteresis), then **5o (#122)** deep-tier orphaned kit demands.

## Laws (TODO §3 — enforce on yourself)
- Commit ONLY with a pathspec on the commit itself (`git commit -m ... -- <files>`; `git add <new files>` first for untracked). Post-commit hook auto-pushes; if you see a ref-lock rejection, `git fetch` and confirm origin/main matches HEAD before doing anything else. Commit messages end with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
- NEVER prefix a Bash command with `cd /home/felix/ghq/... &&` — it forwards a permission prompt to Felix's screen. Your shell already runs in the repo; use absolute paths or `git -C`.
- OWNER=engine-dev-3 PURPOSE="..." on every spawn; DECIDER_EXCLUDE=1 on test bots; ./list.sh first; stop your bots when done. - Ack-before-edit on any file outside your lane (survival.js/telemetry.js/metrics/bench graders = engine-dev; SCOREBOARD race sections = test-driver). Wall-clock timers are the lead's. FEEDBACK.md append-only. Food-scarcity tests inject state (auto-eat's watcher eats first).
- Report to the lead at every task boundary (commit hash, what verified how, what you argued against). Report design BEFORE code when a task touches the SHELTER/REFLEX boundary or changes a contract.
Start with the one-line "alive, resuming 5p" message to the lead, then 5p.
</teammate-message>

## 3. Tonight's laws & doctrines (enforce from spawn prompt #6 above)
- THE HUMAN BAR (GOAL.md): playcheck PLAYING + direction-gate PASS + survives night unaided +
  human trail — all four on one hour.
- Composition rot: "an unverified deferral is a disablement wearing a shortcut's clothing" (+ the
  refinement: an INSTRUMENTED deferral under measurement is a hypothesis, not rot).
- Zero defense must be unrepresentable (routing must always reach a branch that CAN act).
- Every iterative search needs an anchor; assumed-false ≠ verified-false (representable uncertainty);
- Instrument is scorekeeper; predictions get scored AT the prediction; deferred-gap comments are
  promissory notes (two honored tonight); ensureTool is NOT test-inert by default (opts.depot:false
  in fixtures); a TODO comment is not a tracker item.

- **Shared-index commit law** (2026-09-03, learned by a race): everyone commits on ONE working tree, so `git add X && git commit` commits whatever anyone else has staged. Commit with a pathspec on the commit itself: `git commit -m ... -- <files>` (or `git commit <files>`), never a bare `git commit`.

- **Push discipline**: every commit auto-pushes via .git/hooks/post-commit (installed 2026-09-02 after 113 commits sat unpushed for a day). If a clone lacks the hook, `git push` after every commit is law; check .git/push.log if GitHub looks stale.

- **Reading teammate progress (tmux mode)**: the pane prompt line is NOT a liveness signal (it shows an empty prompt while the model thinks). Use ListAgents (running/idle) + context growth in the pane status bar + `git status`/commits. Inbox files under ~/.claude/teams/<session>/inboxes/ show undelivered messages (empty = consumed).

- **Soak-window world hygiene** (learned 2026-09-03, soak #4): during a formal soak window NO other bot may run on the soak server within 200 blocks of the soak bot — DECIDER_EXCLUDE protects only the LLM budget; a test bot digging near the soak bot's work sites corrupts the trail criterion. Test elsewhere (another server/world) or after the window. Grader tooling: trail.mjs/humanbar4.mjs `--exclude-zones "x,z,r"` for any contamination that did happen, recorded in the gate file. Caught live on GrantigGustav (gear-race run #7, world-race7), concluding the run via DEAD RACE = DEAD STOP (Felix's
law): position, HP, and food all held EXACTLY flat for 5+ consecutive minutes (12:34:08Z → 12:39:14Z+) with a
diagnosed cause and no legal `setProject` recovery.

**Mechanism, verbatim from `__skills.status(bot,0)`'s own log and structured fields at the moment of conclusion**:
```
danger: {"score":2.2,"state":"panic","threats":[{"name":"creeper","d":15,"s":1.13,"los":false,"ranged":false,
  "id":3952,"pos":[-90,75,-62]}]}
survival: {"state":"panic:deciding","branch":"WALL_OFF","fires":15,"recovered":13,"failures":1,"standdown":null}
bot: {"pos":[-95,73,-76],"hp":6.8,"food":16,"dim":"overworld","held":{"name":"dirt","count":7},
  "light":0,"rawLight":0,"skyLight":0,"surfaceExposed":false}
log tail: 'danger panic (1.94): creeper at 16.3' -> 'panic_enter (danger) hp=7 threat=creeper at 16.3' ->
  'panic_recovered branch=WALL_OFF hp=7 — driver decides resume vs abort' -> (repeat, distance oscillating
  13.6-16.3, `los` never true, `ranged` never true) x 15 fires over ~15 minutes total, the last several minutes
  with zero other activity at all.
```
The bot is fully sealed underground (`surfaceExposed:false`, all three light fields 0 — genuinely enclosed, not a
sensor artifact) holding only `dirt x7` (its own WALL_OFF filler). A creeper 13-16 blocks away, never in line of
sight, never ranged (creepers have no ranged attack regardless), is re-triggering `danger.state:panic` every
cycle — `pick()`'s own danger-scoring apparently treats raw distance-based proximity as sufficient for `panic`
regardless of whether the threat could plausibly reach the bot (walled in, no LOS, no path). Each `panic_enter` ->
`WALL_OFF` -> `panic_recovered` cycle completes in isolation (WALL_OFF "succeeds" — the bot IS walled in already)
but nothing ever declares the incident over, because the SAME distant creeper is still "detected" on the very
next tick. `#96`'s zero-defense floor and `#100`'s post-victory standdown are not implicated — this isn't a
combat loss or noisy chat spam, it's the danger-detection layer itself refusing to downgrade from `panic` for a
threat that was never actually credible.

**Why no `setProject` could fix it**: no `needs_direction` episode opens for most of this cycle (`direction.state`
stayed `cooldown` for the bulk of the 5-minute window) — the decider never sees a decision point either. One
episode DID open late (`dmtlihbe06`, `project_stalled`, 12:38:48Z) and the decider answered in ~20s with
`chopTrees` (dispatch mechanically correct, `#109`'s fast-answer behavior working exactly as designed) — but
REFLEX (this panic loop) outranks `PROJECT` in the rung ladder, so the dispatch was immediately re-preempted on
the very next `panic_enter`. This is structurally the same shape as `#112`'s standdown-carryover finding
(a lower-priority rung's fresh instruction getting swallowed by a higher-priority rung that won't release) but
one tier up the ladder and with a different root cause (REFLEX's OWN fire condition never clearing, not a stale
backoff timer).

**Not filing a proposed fix shape** (survival.js/dangerscan.js, eng-3's lane) — candidates worth eng-3 evaluating,
not proposed as verified: (a) `pick()`'s panic-entry condition should probably require SOME plausible path to the
bot (LOS, or a ranged capability, or proximity below some threshold that accounts for solid terrain between);
(b) alternatively, `panic_recovered`'s "driver decides resume vs abort" framing suggests the ORIGINAL design
intent was for something (a driver, or an automatic policy) to explicitly resolve "is this really over" rather
than silently re-entering on the next tick — if that resolution step was never wired up, this may be a genuine
missing mechanism, not just a scoring threshold tuned wrong.

**Driver response**: held all `setProject` calls once the pattern was clear (a redirect couldn't reach PROJECT
while REFLEX kept reclaiming it) rather than spamming ineffective steering calls. Concluded DNF at wood (stone
never reached this run — the bot was still mid-excursion when this loop began) via DEAD RACE = DEAD STOP, per
team-lead's explicit agreement this met the rule's own terms. **Not stopping the bot** — team-lead's instruction:

(-95,73,-76)), decider left running, for live forensics against a real, reproducible instance of the loop.

5m design (before code, per §3 — this touches the SHELTER boundary). survival.js is currently clean in the tree; still waiting on engine-dev's go-ahead (messaged them, no reply yet), designing in parallel so I'm ready the moment they clear it.

Plan: inside shelterEnter()'s existing wait loop (survival.js ~1375-1406), when built.kind==='digin' && built.sealed:
- At loop entry (once): capture hasPickaxe = bot.inventory.items().some(i=>/pickaxe$/.test(i.name)) (matches skills.js's own `/pickaxe$/.test(held)` convention) and batchesUsed=0. require('./nightmine.js') defensively, same idiom as foods.js.
- Each loop iteration, AFTER the existing exit checks (exitRequested/threatsNow/dawn/starving/health<=0) and BEFORE the sleep: if no nightmine task is currently running (`!(__skills.currentTask && __skills.currentTask.running)`) — either nothing dispatched yet, or the last dispatch just ended — decide:
  - task just ended with error.code==='not_found' and more targets left in nightMineTargets() order (coal_ore -> iron_ore -> stone): dispatch the next target immediately, same batch (doesn't consume the batch-cap — a fast not_found scan is cheap, matches nightmine.js's own header comment).
  - task ended (done, or a real non-not_found error/timeout), or nothing dispatched yet: call shouldNightMine({builtKind, builtSealed, hasPickaxe, currentY: bot.entity.position.y, freeSlots: bot.inventory.emptySlotCount(), batchesUsed}) fresh; if go, dispatch nightMineTargets()[0] via __skills.start(bot,'mineLane', nightMineArgs(target, built.restY)), batchesUsed++ when a batch (not a not_found retry) completes.
  - task still running: do nothing — the loop's own poll cadence IS the concurrency, no separate timer needed.
- Tighten the loop's sleep(500)->sleep(300) so exit conditions (esp. threatsNow()) are checked at 300ms even mid-batch.
- On ANY exit condition firing while a nightmine task is in flight: call __skills.stop('shelter:nightmine') immediately (before break), so mineLane's next per-block checkpoint cancels within ~1s, then fall into the existing shelterExitBuild/exit sequence unchanged.
- laneY stays nightmine.js's own restY-1 (never touched) — seal is never reopened upward, that safety property lives in the args, not in my wiring.
- Hut variant (built.kind==='hut') untouched — no branch added there.

Will add a bench/fixtures case (sealed digin + night + hasPickaxe -> mineLane dispatched; threat mid-batch -> stopped + existing exit fires; dawn -> exit, never re-seals) and live-verify per your brief (RCON night on 25599, sealed dig-in, batch banks stone, summoned threat interrupts within ~1s, seal never opens upward). Any objection before I start once engine-dev clears the file?

Follow-up on 5m (still waiting on your survival.js clearance — no rush, just adding detail while I wait): lead ACK'd the design with one addition — a `night_mine` ledger event through the two-surface pattern (pushLog + telemetry), same shape as M.panic, so soak #6's stall attribution can show "SHELTER-owned but mining" instead of "SHELTER idle."

Shape: `{ev:'night_mine', op:'start'|'batch_done'|'stopped', target, blocks, reason, batchesUsed, pos}`
- start: fired when a mineLane batch is dispatched — target ('coal_ore'|'iron_ore'|'stone'), batchesUsed (count so far this shelter session)
- batch_done: fired when a dispatch completes cleanly (done, or a real non-not_found terminal error) — adds blocks (count mined, from task.collected/result)
- stopped: fired when an exit condition (threat/dawn/hunger/dead/exitRequested) interrupts an in-flight batch — reason = the exit condition name, blocks = whatever partial count is available

I'm planning to call `globalThis.__metrics.emit('night_mine', {...})` DIRECTLY (M.emit is already public API, telemetry.js:175) rather than add a new M.nightMine wrapper — avoids touching telemetry.js at all, which is your lane. Flag if you'd rather have a dedicated M.nightMine(op, ...) wrapper for consistency with M.panic's shape (I'd leave that edit to you either way). Your grader can key off `ev==='night_mine'` + `op` either way.

### 2026-09-03 engine-dev — #121 (TODO 5r) panic re-entry loop on a never-actionable threat: fixed, live-verified against the specimen; a git-attribution mistake noted honestly

New HIGH item from the lead, gates soak #6: test-driver's run #7 racer (GrantigGustav) stuck
6.5+ minutes in panic_enter -> WALL_OFF -> panic_recovered -> re-enter on a creeper at 13-16
blocks, los:false, ranged:false — not visible, not shooting, doing nothing. HP pinned at 6.77
the entire time; no direction episode ever opened because WALL_OFF kept reporting "recovered",
so the driver never saw a stall to escalate.

Root cause, confirmed by reading dangerscan.js directly (not guessed): `panicNow()` is
`score>=5 OR hp<hpPanic(8) OR creeper<=8blocks`. The creeper's own score (1.98) never came
close to 5 — the actual trigger was the bot's OWN hp sitting below 8, a separate OR'd
condition unrelated to the creeper at all. The real bug: every "is danger genuinely over"
check in survival.js (#92's heal-deadlock escape inside branchWallOff's own wait loop, its
`threatClear` return field, and standdown's arm/re-clear checks in `enter()`) gates on
`threatsNow().length === 0` — and the distant, unseen creeper's mere PRESENCE in dangerscan's
raw list permanently blocked every one of them from ever reading true, even though it could
neither see nor reach the bot. So standdown never armed despite `cannotHeal()` being genuinely
true the whole time (food stuck at 16, no food item held), and dangerscan's hp<8 term kept
re-forcing panic on a threat that was never actually the problem.

Two fixes landed, both explicitly requested:
1. New `actionableThreats()` (`los===true || d<=12`) swapped into the four "is it genuinely
   over" call sites above. `threatsNow()` itself and `pick()`'s own creeper(d<=8)/ranged(&&los)
   dispatch gates are untouched — already tighter, unaffected.
2. Generic `g.panicStreak`, keyed on dangerscan's raw top threat id, independent of which
   branch handles it: 3 consecutive panic cycles against the same threat id with zero damage
   taken escalates to a new `branchWalkOff()` (moves 24 blocks directly away from the threat's
   last known position, bounded 8s) instead of repeating. Belt-and-suspenders alongside fix 1.

via `jq -Rs '{code:.}' survival.js | POST /eval` (same idempotent-reinject pattern as
inject.sh, just applied to survival.js instead of skills.js) into GrantigGustav (port 3161,
25600). Confirmed: fires/recovered reset on injection, exactly ONE panic cycle ran afterward
(not a repeat), standdown armed correctly with the honest message ("Walled off but can't
heal — food stuck at 16/20 with nothing to eat. Standing down at 3 HP. Need food or new
orders."), and the bot resumed its normal REFLEX/chopTrees agenda work instead of looping.
A later GENUINE new hp drop (6.77->2.77, real damage from the resumed work) correctly broke
through standdown once, was handled, and re-armed — confirms the fix suppresses only the
phantom loop, not real re-triggers. Gave the specimen 8 bread via RCON afterward so it isn't
left hungry; it's currently safely sealed/stood-down waiting on food or orders (getting it to
actually eat while stood down is agenda/EAT-rung territory, not survival.js's — not chased
further, out of lane).

specimen rather than a synthetic scenario, per the lead's explicit ask to test on it before
committing. Flagging in case soak #6 wants a regression fixture for actionableThreats/
panicStreak before it gates further work.

work (shelterEnter() night-mining wiring) was ALSO uncommitted in the same survival.js working

5m-b design (before code, SHELTER boundary). Investigated why both live deaths happened, and it changes which of your two options I'm picking.

Root cause of the race: survival.js's REFLEX trigger is NOT gated by shelterEnter()'s own loop at all — dangerscan.js runs its own scan every 250ms and calls `onDanger()` -> `enter('danger')` directly the instant `dangerState` flips to panic (survival.js:1894), independently of my loop's poll. Both live death logs confirm this fired FIRST both times ("task: stop requested: panic" landed before my own "night_mine stopped (threat)" line). My loop polls at 300ms — no faster, and even at equal cadence there's no ordering guarantee between two independent timers. So "plug the mouth BEFORE yielding to REFLEX" as a REACTIVE race (detect threat -> retreat -> plug -> then yield) is not reliably winnable — confirmed by both trials landing the loss the same way.

Going with your alternative instead, hardened: PROACTIVE, not reactive. After EVERY batch (not just on a threat), before evaluating the next one: walk back to the chamber (the original dig-in resting position, never changes — straight-down dig) and reseal all 4 side cells at both heights with the cobblestone it just mined (same `placeAt` primitive shelterHut/shelterDigIn already use, so it's proven code, not new primitives). Next batch digs back out through its own reseal to continue. This means the bot is genuinely sealed for the entire BETWEEN-batch window — most of the timeline — with no race to win, since nothing needs to detect anything first. Also shrinking the per-batch footprint (count 6->2, maxDist 8->4) to shrink the residual MID-batch exposure window. On top of that, my loop's own threatsNow() check still attempts a best-effort retreat+reseal on a live catch, but only when `__survival.active` isn't already true (so it never fights an in-flight WALL_OFF for pathfinder/dig control — backs off cleanly if REFLEX already claimed it).

Trade-off: costs real mining efficiency (constant reseal/re-dig every batch) and consumes filler each cycle — always available (cobblestone is what's being mined) but worth flagging since it's a real efficiency hit in exchange for safety, which matches your framing (safety over throughput here).

Fixture: bench-level hermetic check of the reseal decision logic, plus the same live protocol as 5m (RCON night, summoned threat), now checking hpMin/survival across 3 repeated trials with the threat approaching from a set distance (not teleported on top of the bot — that's not a realistic scenario 5m or 5m-b was ever asked to survive).

Announcing to engine-dev now per the rebase rule before touching survival.js. Any objection to the proactive-over-reactive call before I start?

Heads up before I stage: lead assigned me 5m-b (gates soak #6, before 5q) — the two night-mining deaths I flagged are getting fixed in MY lane (shelterEnter() wrapper only, not branchWallOff), so you don't need to touch anything for it. I'll be editing survival.js again shortly (proactive reseal-between-batches + a best-effort retreat on threat detection that explicitly backs off if `__survival.active` is already true, so it won't fight your branchFleeAway/WALL_OFF work for pathfinder control). Let me know when you're at a safe commit point on your LOS-bias work and I'll rebase on top before staging, same as last time. No rush — just don't want another accidental cross-stage.

### 2026-09-03 engine-dev-3 — TODO 5q (#125): EAT/REFLEX ownership thrash — hysteresis landed, hermetically verified

engine-dev's own #121/5n FEEDBACK entry flagged a rung-sequence THRASH — "EAT_CRITICAL REFLEX
EAT REFLEX EAT" — surfaced once BREAK_LOS survived long enough for hunger-driven EAT cycling to
manifest during a sustained encounter. Root cause, read from `choose()`/REFLEX's own fire()/
clear(): REFLEX's `fire()` (`survivalActive || (dangerState==='panic' && !panicStale)`) and
`clear()` are exact logical complements, so the instant `survivalActive` drops false between two
panic runs (survival.js's own "driver decides resume vs abort" gap), REFLEX releases INSTANTLY
that same tick — and since `choose()`'s owner-latch only re-checks the CURRENT owner's clear(),
never re-runs a lower rung's own fire() while latched, a hungry bot's EAT rung grabs ownership
the moment that gap opens, only to lose it again just as instantly the next tick REFLEX's fire()
flips back true (prio 0 always preempts unconditionally, by design — confirmed correct and NOT
touched here, see below). The EXISTING anti-flap floor (`MIN_SWITCH_MS`, `choose()`'s own
comment "anti-flap floor, safety rungs exempt") does not cover this: it keys off how long the
CURRENT owner has held the body, and a real REFLEX episode easily exceeds MIN_SWITCH_MS before
it finally clears, so the floor is already satisfied by the time EAT would grab it, and the
reverse direction (EAT->REFLEX) is deliberately never floored (REFLEX must always win instantly
— multiple prior FEEDBACK entries argue this hard, not reopening it).

Fix, scoped narrowly: `A.reflexClearSince` (agenda.js v37->v38) timestamps the last REAL tick()
transition OFF a REFLEX owner (stamped in `tick()`, same convention as the existing `A.calmSince`
— real A state, not part of the injected dry-run snapshot). EAT's (prio 4, food<=17, a routine
top-up) `fire()` gains `&& (A.reflexClearSince === 0 || (s.now - A.reflexClearSince) >=

food ladder's one true emergency rung (#117's own doctrine: "no engine-internal escape... only
REFLEX/POSTURE may ever preempt it"), and delaying it risks real starvation harm in exchange for
a smoother-looking log line. The observed live trace mixed EAT_CRITICAL into the thrash too, so
this fix does not eliminate every hop in that exact sequence — it targets the hop that is safe to
suppress (EAT) and leaves the emergency hop (EAT_CRITICAL) exactly as aggressive as #117 made it,
by design, not as an oversight.

One real gotcha caught before landing: `TICK_MS` is 2000 and `choose()` only runs once per tick
— a dwell SHORTER than one tick interval can never actually suppress anything, since by the next
`choose()` call at least `TICK_MS` has already elapsed regardless of the dwell's own value. First
draft used 1500ms (matching `MIN_SWITCH_MS`'s existing magnitude) and would have been a complete

exercises the real tick interval). Settled on `EAT_REFLEX_DWELL_MS = 4000` (two full ticks,

5m-b status: built and mechanically verified, but honestly NOT at 3/3 alive yet — reporting before committing rather than rounding up.

Built (survival.js v16->v17): proactive reseal after every batch (walk to chamber, placeAt the 8 nightMineResealCells candidates, no-ops on whatever's solid), batch footprint shrunk 6/8→1/2, and a second fix I found necessary along the way: shelterExitBuild's own cap-dig was fighting REFLEX/WALL_OFF for pathfinder/dig control on a threat exit ("shelter exit dig failed: Digging aborted") — now skipped entirely when exitReason==='threat'. Also added a reactive path: when MY OWN threatsNow() check wins the race against dangerscan's independent onDanger trigger (checked via g.active), it retreats+reseals immediately instead of leaving the bot standing exposed.

4 live trials (real NoAI:0b zombie, RCON-summoned mid-batch), each after a fix landed:
1. First cut: REFLEX won the race, shelterExitBuild fought it, WALL_OFF got 4 open faces → death.
2. After the exit-skip fix: MY check won the race this time (g.active false) but I hadn't yet added the reactive reseal — bot stood exposed ~4s until REFLEX engaged → death.
3. After adding the reactive reseal: REFLEX won the race again, correctly backed off (no fight) — WALL_OFF still only got to 2 open faces → death.
4. After shrinking footprint to count:1/maxDist:2: WALL_OFF actually HELD the first engagement (hp 20→15, recovered) — then the zombie re-engaged 502ms later ("still actionable") and finished it on the second wave.

Trend is real (4-6 open faces → 2 → one wave survived) but not a guarantee. Root cause of what's left: WALL_OFF's own box-sealing math against a real, persistent, actively-pursuing NoAI:0b mob in a 1-wide corridor/partial-chamber shape — that's downstream of my dispatch, in survival.js's panic/WALL_OFF territory you said isn't mine to fix. Sanity-checked with NoAI:1b too (matching #119's own precedent that NoAI:0b carries real combat RNG) — confirmed my mechanics (stop/skip-exit/reseal ledger events) all fire correctly, but NoAI:1b never deals damage at all so it can't tell me anything about survival odds specifically.

Your call: (a) accept this as a bounded, documented improvement (same shape as #121/5n's FLEE_AWAY-bare-platform "non-gating loss" precedent) and I commit+FEEDBACK it as-is with the honest trial data, or (b) this needs an ACK'd, scoped extension into branchWallOff's own corridor-sealing (engine-dev's file, would need their sign-off) before it can call 3/3. Not committing until I hear back — didn't want to either sit on real, working improvements indefinitely or round up an incomplete result to "done."
